name: Cafesjian Center for the Arts
funding: Run by the Cafesjian Museum Foundation, which Gerard Cafesjian endowed with over $35M from his West Publishing fortune. Exhibits draw on the Cafesjian Art Trust.
watch: Cafesjian died in 2013. His 2007 to 2011 lawsuit with the Armenian Assembly ended with the court finding he acted in good faith.
records_note: The Cafesjian pages name Gerard Cafesjian as principal benefactor but publish no reports, accounts, sponsor list or board.

name: Samstag Museum of Art
funding: Adelaide University museum, founded in 2007 by the University of South Australia. The Samstag bequest funds scholarships it administers. Partners: Adelaide Festival, Adelaide Film Festival, The Lane Vineyard.
watch: A 2024 encampment targeted the University of Adelaide, then a separate university from the museum's own.
records_note: Samstag shows partner logos without dates and names a seven-person board; no annual report or accounts were found, and the university's Council is listed.

name: Murray Art Museum Albury
funding: AlburyCity Council and Create NSW. Major benefactors: Paul Ramsay Foundation, Russell Mills Foundation, Metal Manufacturers and the Colin and Lorraine Joss family. MAMA Art Foundation raises acquisition funds.
watch: MAMA Ltd was formed in July 2023 to take over from the council, which still supports it.
records_note: MAMA's Art Foundation posts reports for 2022/23 to 2024/25 and names its committee; donors are listed by tier, undated; its parent council posts audited accounts.

name: Art Gallery of Ballarat
funding: 150,607 visitors (2023-24); City of Ballarat with Creative Victoria; Ian Potter, Sidney Myer, Buckland, Helen Macpherson Smith, Gandel; McCain, Mars, NAB.
watch: UNVERIFIED: Exhibition sponsors unverified. Caltex (fuel retailer, now Ampol) sits on the cumulative Major Gifts roll; gift date not stated.
records_note: Ballarat has an Our donors page and no reports of its own; its parent City of Ballarat posts annual reports 2013/14 to 2024/25.

name: Bendigo Art Gallery
funding: $45M redevelopment (2025): $21M Victoria, $9M City of Greater Bendigo, Sidney Myer Fund $4M, Ian Potter $3M; partners La Trobe University, Innes, Balgownie, Mercure.
watch: UNVERIFIED: Sponsors page blocked. Closed Dec 2025 to early 2028 for redevelopment. A $15M federal Growing Regions bid was rejected Jan 2025 on an administrative issue, not programming.
records_note: bendigoregion.com.au returned HTTP 403; search lists gallery annual reports for 2020 to 2025 and a Gallery Board page, none opened.

name: QAGOMA
funding: 1.17M visits (2024-25); Queensland Government statutory body; Creative Australia, Shayher Group, Carnival Cruise Line, Tim Fairfax Family Foundation.
watch: Carnival Corporation, parent of Carnival Cruise Line, paid $40M for oily-waste dumping in 2016 and $20M in 2019 for probation violations.
records_note: Publishes statutory annual reports with financial statements and trustees back to 1991-92; the main site blocked checks of its donor pages.

name: Cairns Art Gallery
funding: Cairns Regional Council gives 55 to 60 percent of operating costs. Cairns Art Gallery Foundation and Double R Arts Foundation fund works and artists. Cairns RSL Club funded 12 fellowships.
watch: Cairns RSL Club runs a gaming venue and funded fellowship rounds in 2021 and 2022. Double R founders are not named.
why_flagged: Cairns Regional Council gives 55 to 60 percent of operating costs. Cairns Art Gallery Foundation and Double R Arts Foundation fund works and artists. Cairns RSL Club funded 12 fellowships.
records_note: The gallery's own site posts nothing, but the ACNC register holds its reports and 2014 to 2025 accounts and names nine directors.

name: Geelong Gallery
funding: Revenue A$2.85M (2024-25) with grants A$1.67M, from the City of Greater Geelong and the Victorian Government, and sponsorship A$41k. Donors include the Ian Potter, Brookes, Archibald and Trawalla foundations.
watch: Nearly 70,000 visitors in 2024-25. The cited partners page dates from 2020-21; the annual report is current.
records_note: Posts six annual reports with audited accounts, names donors in the 2024-25 report and lists its board; the partners page is from 2020-21.

name: Buxton Contemporary
funding: Opened 2018 on a gift of the building and collection from Michael and Janet Buxton (property). Run within the University of Melbourne's museums.
watch: A 2024 student encampment at the University of Melbourne targeted the university's arms investments, not the museum, so it adds no flag.
records_note: Buxton posts no reports of its own; parent University of Melbourne tabled a 2024 annual report. Buxton names Circle supporters, undated, and lists no board.

name: Gertrude Contemporary
funding: Creative Victoria, the federal Visual Arts, Craft and Design Framework and City of Darebin. Donors include Michael and Janet Buxton, Proclaim, and the Mori Provan and Tucker foundations.
watch: Proclaim has sponsored the Octopus exhibition since 2002. No flagged-industry funder.
records_note: Posts annual reports for 2023 to 2025 with a financial report and names board members; its supporters page names donors without a date.

name: Monash University Museum of Art
funding: University-funded; Besen family built the 2010 Caulfield premises; Ian Potter Sculpture Court commissions; media partner Schwartz Media; MUMA Contemporaries from $1,000.
watch: UNVERIFIED: Support page blocked. Censorship row: Monash indefinitely postponed Stolon Press: Flat earth (Khaled Sabsabi) on 25 Mar 2025 under pressure; reopened 29 May 2025.
records_note: MUMA posts no reports of its own; parent Monash University publishes an annual report with accounts, and MUMA names donors on its support pages.

name: Potter Museum of Art
funding: University of Melbourne. Reopened May 2025 with the Ian Potter Foundation and Lady Primrose Potter; exhibition backers Peter and Ruth McMullin, Naomi Milgrom, the Zhangs and the Gordon Darling Foundation.
watch: A 2024 student encampment at the University of Melbourne targeted the university's arms investments, not the museum, so it adds no flag.
records_note: The Potter posts no reports of its own; parent University of Melbourne tabled a 2024 annual report. A 2024 release names its donors.
